newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares ease 0.03 pct in quiet business.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares ease 0.03 pct in quiet business.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell again on Sunday in quiet business dominated by trade in blue-chip Arab Bank Group, brokers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.05 points to 147.63 points, maintaining a gradual slide from just under 148 at the start of the month.

Despite the fall, brokers tried to remain upbeat about the market, dormant since early October as pessimism over lack of trade with sanction-hit Iraq to the east and Palestinians to the west compounded domestic factors hampering the bourse.
"Local investors are expecting positive things now," said Nasser al-Amad, general manager of United Financial Investment. "All the negatives things have been factored in."
He said the low turnover showed there was no stampede to sell shares despite the consistent downward trend on the index.
"The market is in its bottom level now," Amad said. "We don't have anyone willing to sell."

Brokers say that, with the Central Bank pledged to maintain high interest rates to protect the Jordanian dinar, they are looking instead for progress in Palestinian-Israeli talks to boost sentiment. Any sign of increased trade in food or pharmaceuticals to Iraq would also help the market.
Trade in Arab Bank accounted for nearly half of Sunday's 514,000 dinar ($726,000) turnover. The stock closed unchanged at 246 dinars.

"There is high demand on this share," said Amad. "It is a very safe investment tool." The bank is expected to announce a share split and a capital increase as soon as the government passes a new companies law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.
Trade in most other stocks was extremely shallow, with the five biggest gainers boasting a combined turnover of less than 10,000 dinars.
Overall eight shares rose, 14 fell and 18 were traded but closed unchanged from Saturday.
